title: Free Write
description: An open-ended writing space. No prompt, no structure — just write.

title: The Thesis-Driven Essay
description: This course will show you how to write a thesis-driven critical essay. Learn how to find your focus, develop a thesis statement, organize body paragraphs, and write a compelling conclusion. Write an essay that amazes your readers!

categories.label: Thesis/Content
categories.description: Original, defensible thesis with sustained critical thinking and meaningful deductions.

categories.label: Organization/Structure
categories.description: Purposeful structure with strong progression, clear transitions, and a conclusion that extends thinking.

categories.label: Evidence/Support
categories.description: Precise, well-integrated evidence that deepens analysis and builds authority.

categories.label: Voice/Style
categories.description: Authentic voice with engaging, precise language and consistent tone.

categories.label: Grammar/Syntax/Formatting
categories.description: Technical correctness and polished presentation that support clarity.

gradingCalibrationNotes: Represents the pre-existing Yawp thesis-driven essay grading assistant path.

title: The 5-Paragraph Essay
description: In this course, students learn the basic, fundamental form for academic writing.

title: Welcome to YAWP!
description: Get familiar with the YAWP! platform and Tutor.

title: Daily Pages
description: Create entries for daily writing assignments or reflections, or use it to develop your next big idea.

title: GBA 300
description: International Expansion Plan — create a firm and prepare a report to present to CEO-level executives that offers a recommendation for expanding into a new international market.

title: ACT Writing Section
description: Practice the ACT Writing Section and get real feedback on how to improve.

categories.label: Ideas and Analysis
categories.description: Evaluate the clarity of the writer's perspective and analysis of the relationships among perspectives.

categories.label: Development and Support
categories.description: Evaluate how well claims are developed with reasoning, examples, and implications.

categories.label: Organization
categories.description: Evaluate purposeful sequencing, paragraphing, transitions, and control of the response.

categories.label: Language Use and Conventions
categories.description: Evaluate word choice, sentence control, grammar, usage, and mechanics as they affect clarity.

gradingPromptConfigJson.scoreInstructions: Scores must be integers 1-6 for each ACT domain. The app converts the average domain score to a 2-12 ACT-style composite for display.
gradingPromptConfigJson.rubricInstructions: Score the four ACT Writing domains independently. Focus first on Ideas and Analysis and Development and Support. Language Use and Conventions matters when errors impede clarity.
gradingPromptConfigJson.systemInstructions: Grade this as ACT Writing with four rubric domains. Do not use thesis-driven essay categories. Give concise retrospective feedback for each ACT domain.
